id: Practice Direction 72 – Third Party Debt Orders
content:
# PRACTICE DIRECTION 72 – THIRD PARTY DEBT ORDERS

# This Practice Direction supplements Part 72

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72] Contents of this Practice Direction

## Application notice – rule 72.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Application notice – rule 72.3] 1.1 An application for a third party debt order must be made by filing an application notice in Practice Form N349 .

## 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (1) the name and address of the judgment debtor;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (2) details of the judgment or order sought to be enforced;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (3) the amount of money remaining due under the judgment or order;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (4) if the judgment debt is payable by instalments, the amount of any instalments which have fallen due and remain unpaid;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (5) the name and address of the third party;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (6) if the third party is a bank or building society –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (a) its name and the address of the branch at which the judgment debtor’s account is believed to be held; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (b) the account number;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] or, if the judgment creditor does not know all or part of this information, that fact;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (7) confirmation that to the best of the judgment creditor’s knowledge or belief the third party –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (a) is within the jurisdiction; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (b) owes money to or holds money to the credit of the judgment debtor;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (8) if the judgment creditor knows or believes that any person other than the judgment debtor has any claim to the money owed by the third party –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (a) his name and (if known) his address; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (b) such information as is known to the judgment creditor about his claim;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (9) details of any other applications for third party debt orders issued by the judgment creditor in respect of the same judgment debt; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] (10) the sources or grounds of the judgment creditor’s knowledge or belief of the matters referred to in (7), (8) and (9).

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 1.2 The application notice must contain the following information –] 1.3 The court will not grant speculative applications for third party debt orders, and will only make an interim third party debt order against a bank or building society if the judgment creditor’s application notice contains evidence to substantiate his belief that the judgment debtor has an account with the bank or building society in question.

## Interim third party debt order – rule 72.4

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Interim third party debt order – rule 72.4] 2 An interim third party debt order will specify the amount of money which the third party must retain (rule 72.4(3)). This will include, in respect of the judgment creditor’s fixed costs of the application, the amount which would be allowed to the judgment creditor under rule 45.23 if the whole balance of the judgment debt were recovered.

## Interim orders relating to bank or building society accounts – rule 72.6(1)–(3)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Interim orders relating to bank or building society accounts – rule 72.6(1)–(3)] 3.1 A bank or building society served with an interim third party debt order is only required by rule 72.6, unless the order states otherwise –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Interim orders relating to bank or building society accounts – rule 72.6(1)–(3)] (1) to retain money in accounts held solely by the judgment debtor (or, if there are joint judgment debtors, accounts held jointly by them or solely by either or any of them); and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Interim orders relating to bank or building society accounts – rule 72.6(1)–(3)] (2) to search for and disclose information about such accounts.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Interim orders relating to bank or building society accounts – rule 72.6(1)–(3)] 3.2 The bank or building society is not required, for example, to retain money in, or disclose information about –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Interim orders relating to bank or building society accounts – rule 72.6(1)–(3)] (1) accounts in the joint names of the judgment debtor and another person; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Interim orders relating to bank or building society accounts – rule 72.6(1)–(3)] (2) if the interim order has been made against a firm, accounts in the names of individual members of that firm.

## Attachment of debts owed by a partnership

## 3A.1 This paragraph relates to debts due or accruing due to a judgment creditor from a partnership.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 3A.1 This paragraph relates to debts due or accruing due to a judgment creditor from a partnership.] 3A.2 An interim third party debt order under rule 72.4(2) relating to such debts must be served on –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 3A.1 This paragraph relates to debts due or accruing due to a judgment creditor from a partnership.] (1) a member of the partnership within the jurisdiction;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 3A.1 This paragraph relates to debts due or accruing due to a judgment creditor from a partnership.] (2) a person authorised by a partner; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 3A.1 This paragraph relates to debts due or accruing due to a judgment creditor from a partnership.] (3) some other person having the control or management of the partnership business.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 3A.1 This paragraph relates to debts due or accruing due to a judgment creditor from a partnership.] 3A.3 Where an order made under rule 72.4(2) requires a partnership to appear before the court, it will be sufficient for a partner to appear before the court.

## Transfer

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Transfer] 4 The court may, on an application by a judgment debtor who wishes to oppose an application for a third party debt order, transfer it to—

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Transfer] (a) in the High Court, the court for the district; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Transfer] (b) in the County Court, the County Court hearing centre serving the address, where the judgment debtor resides carries on business, or to another court.

## Applications for hardship payment orders – rule 72.7

## 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (1) in the proceedings in which the interim third party debt order was made; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (2) under the same claim number,

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] regardless of where the judgment debtor makes the application.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] 5.2 An application for a hardship payment order will be dealt with by the court to which it is made.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (Rule 72.7(2) provides that an application may be made –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] in High Court proceedings, in the Royal Courts of Justice or to any district registry; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] in County Court proceedings, to any County Court hearing centre.)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] 5.3 If the application is made to a different court from that dealing with the application for a third party debt order –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (1) the application for a third party debt order will not be transferred; but

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (2) the court dealing with that application will send copies of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (a) the application notice; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (b) the interim third party debt order

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] to the court hearing the application for a hardship payment order

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] 5.4 Rule 72.7(3) requires an application for a hardship payment order to be served on the judgment creditor at least 2 days before the court is to deal with the application, unless the court orders otherwise. In cases of exceptional urgency the judgment debtor may apply for a hardship payment order without notice to the judgment creditor and a judge will decide whether to –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (1) deal with the application without it being served on the judgment creditor; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (2) direct it to be served.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] 5.5 If the judge decides to deal with the application without it being served on the judgment creditor, where possible he will normally –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (1) direct that the judgment creditor be informed of the application; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] (2) give him the opportunity to make representations,

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] by telephone, fax or other appropriate method of communication.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > 5.1 The court will treat an application for a hardship payment order as being made –] 5.6 The evidence filed by a judgment debtor in support of an application for a hardship payment order should include documentary evidence, for example (if appropriate) bank statements, wage slips and mortgage statements, to prove his financial position and need for the payment.

## Final orders relating to building society accounts

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 72 > Final orders relating to building society accounts] 6 A final third party debt order will not require a payment which would reduce to less than £1 the amount in a judgment debtor’s account with a building society or credit union.
